reason: This capacitor is only connected between the output node (VOUT1) and an internal node (net44) that otherwise only ties to ground through R2, so it mainly provides frequency compensation/RC filtering rather than setting the DC operating point. Removing it usually leaves the amplifier functional in DC/low-frequency operation, but may reduce stability (more ringing/oscillation) depending on loading and transistor parasitics.
impact_estimate: Low for DC functionality; medium risk for AC stability/transient response.

reason: R3 is a shunt load from the output to ground; in many MOS differential amplifier outputs, the DC output level is primarily determined by active device bias currents and loads, not a large explicit shunt resistor. Deleting it typically has minimal impact if there is already a defined load path elsewhere (e.g., through R0/R1 or following-stage input), but leaving it out can make the output more floating under no-load conditions and can change output bias/current consumption.
impact_estimate: Low to medium (depends on whether VOUT1 otherwise has a defined DC load).

reason: net44 appears only in the R2–C0 branch, forming a damping/compensation network from VOUT1 to ground via C0 and R2. If C0 is removed (or if compensation is not required for your simulation/use-case), R2 becomes non-essential and can be deleted with little effect on core amplification behavior.
impact_estimate: Low if C0 is removed or compensation is not required; otherwise medium (it affects the compensation pole/zero).
